Synopsis:
Reuters surveys six historical episodes in which the US Treasury faced acute financing stress and improvised solutions — from Civil War mass retail bond drives and the 1895 Morgan/Belmont gold syndicate, to WWII yield pegging, early-1960s Operation Twist, 1970s auction reform, and the 1978 Carter foreign-currency bonds. The piece is anchored by a brief contemporary hook: long-dated Treasury yields at their highest since 2007 and national debt above $40 trillion, with Bessent asserting the US can grow out of it. The implicit message is that when conventional financing tools fail, Washington historically invents new ones.
